# wherdr v3 documentation

> wherdr is a web app to start coding agents on herdr-core (hc), follow their work and answer
> them from a phone. Read this index first, then only the section that answers your question.
> Links are relative to the repository root. A section that starts with "Needs:" makes sense only
> with the section it names: read that one too.

## Start here

- [Documentation home](docs/README.md): the list of pages, v3 and v2 only.
- [Overview](docs/overview.md#why-wherdr): what wherdr does for you.
- [How it works](docs/overview.md#how-it-works): wherdr's server, the hc socket, transcripts and the data folder.
- [herdr-core](docs/core.md): what v3 supports on hc, the reference for inventory, terminals and conversations.
- [First launch](docs/quick-start.md#quick-start): build, start and open wherdr, then the first settings.

## Install and update

- [Requirements](docs/installation.md#requirements): hc, Linux or macOS, Node.js 22 and Git.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md#installation): install v3 and run it as a service.
- [Keep it running](docs/installation.md#keep-it-running): run wherdr as a service (a systemd --user unit, a macOS LaunchAgent).
- [On-device dictation files](docs/installation.md#on-device-dictation-files): where the dictation models and read-aloud voices are fetched and kept.
- [Updating](docs/installation.md#updating): update v3 by hand; there is no update banner.
- [Install with an agent](docs/install-with-an-agent.md): ready-to-paste prompts for an agent that installs or updates wherdr.
- [Migrate from v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md): install v3 beside v2 and import its machines and settings; its projects are listed for Alfred.
- [Fall back to v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#fall-back-to-v2): v2 keeps running; on v3, `herdr plugin install|update` and the `curl … | sh` installer change nothing and say how to install v3.
- [What is imported](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#what-is-imported): what the v2 import brings over, and what to redo.
- [Set up your v2 projects with Alfred](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#set-up-your-v2-projects-with-alfred): Alfred's first message offers to bring v2 projects over (machine, template, coordinator, open tasks).
- [Auto-deploy from a build machine](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#auto-deploy-from-a-build-machine): build elsewhere and deploy to the server.
- [Fall back to v2](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#fall-back-to-v2): go back to v2, and [uninstall v3](docs/migrate-from-v2.md#uninstall-v3).
- [Install as an app](docs/phone.md#install-it-as-an-app): add wherdr to a phone's home screen or a desktop browser.
- [App start](docs/phone.md#app-start): Settings › Phone › App start, network first or saved copy first; after an update, a Reload banner and no reload by itself.

## Network and security

- [Tailscale setup](docs/networks.md#recommended-always-on-server--tailscale): reach wherdr from a phone over a tailnet with HTTPS.
- [Other private networks](docs/networks.md#other-private-networks): Headscale, NetBird, ZeroTier or WireGuard instead.
- [Security](docs/security.md#security): who may reach wherdr, the passkey lock and remote-shell risks.
- [Network access](docs/security.md#network-access): which networks wherdr answers, and `WHERDR_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md#configuration): environment variables and the data folder.
- [Settings beside the conversation](docs/configuration.md#settings-beside-the-conversation): on a computer window at least 1280 px wide, Settings opened from a conversation show as a side panel on the linked section, resizable from its left edge (drag, arrows, double-click for the default; width kept on the device); Escape closes it, Open full page keeps the full page; `&target=<id>` scrolls to one setting and outlines it for a few seconds.

## Agent list

- [Agents on herdr-core](docs/home.md#agents-on-herdr-core): the live list, states and their counters (agent rows plus the tab's coordinators), quick answers, the sidebar's order (no sideways scroll: long titles and badges ellipsized, a thin scrollbar), and task agents named after their task (after a restart too), one row per task with a line per agent (role, machine, last message).
- [Alfred](docs/home.md#alfred): wherdr's assistant, its agent (kept until you change it), name, home folder and memory.
- [Coordinators](docs/home.md#coordinators): project coordinator rows under Alfred, with the project's colored key badge, and their menu; a stopped one (its terminal ended) offers to resume its conversation or start a new one; coordinators and Tasks to handle follow the machine tab (a project shows on the tabs holding its machines, Alfred on every tab).
- [Offered agents](docs/home.md#offered-agents): Settings › Agents, which programs every picker offers and in which order.
- [Machines as tabs](docs/home.md#machines-as-tabs): the machine tabs and their counts (rows and coordinators), their groups (deleting one puts its projects back to Automatic), which tabs show a project (its machines', a paused one only while its task runs, or its Shown in; notifications are not filtered, the board only on Follow machine tab), a machine's actions, and the offline machines' line with Reconnect (no machine chips while all are online).
- [New agents and tabs](docs/home.md#new-agents-and-tabs): the New sheet, the + of a space's tabs, and renaming or closing a tab or a space.
- [Search](docs/home.md#search): search agents and conversations.
- [Inventory](docs/core.md#inventory): how terminals are placed in spaces and tabs, and how states are read.
- [Creating terminals and agents, machines](docs/core.md#creating-terminals-and-agents-machines): what the New sheet asks hc to run, and how hc reaches core machines.
- [Agent actions](docs/core.md#agent-actions): the agent's … menu: rename, keep after restart, answers, attachments.

## Conversation, terminal and files

- [Conversation and replies](docs/conversation.md): transcripts, following new messages from the bottom, one-tap answers, choice buttons and live task cards (`task KEY-12`, opens the task's sheet) from a `wherdr` code fence, quoted replies, attachments (shown as chips once sent), dictation, and in-app links (`#/settings?section=…`, `#/board?task=…`), shown as labelled buttons, that open a place in wherdr.
- [Live status cards](docs/conversation.md#live-status-cards): a `wherdr` code fence of `status machine:<key>`, `status quota:claude|codex`, `status pr:<KEY>#<n>` or `status op:<task id>` lines shows live cards from wherdr's own data, refreshed every 15 s on screen, "unavailable" when the source is gone.
- [Places an agent opens for you](docs/conversation.md#places-an-agent-opens-for-you): `wherdr alfred ui open` / `wherdr pm ui open '<in-app link>'` shows a place on the device the user last used on the agent's conversation (Settings side panel on a wide computer, a tappable card otherwise), says where (phone or computer), keeps the card in the reply (```wherdr `open <link>`), only in a turn from the user, changing nothing; `ui open --target <id>` highlights one setting (`ui targets` lists the ids).
- [Buttons an agent puts in its reply](docs/conversation.md#buttons-an-agent-puts-in-its-reply): `wherdr pm ui action resume|step|open <task>` adds a card with *Resume*, the step's own button (*Merge*, *Approve screenshots*) or *Open*; only the user's click runs it (`POST /api/ui/act`, never a token), through the task sheet's handlers, after checking the task still waits the same way (else *This changed since*, nothing runs); only in a turn from the user; the outcome shows on the card (an approved merge not ready yet: approved, merges once ready; a refused step action keeps the button with its reason). Settings: `wherdr alfred setting set <key> <value> --propose` adds a card (before → after, *Show me* highlights it, *Cancel*, *Apply*); only the user's Apply changes it, stale if the setting moved since; Alfred never applies a setting itself. `wherdr pm ui show file <path>|shots <task>` shows a file of the agent's own folder or a task's screenshots (before/after) in the side panel, or a card then a sheet on a phone; it approves nothing.
- [Conversations on hc](docs/core.md#conversations): which agents open on their transcript and how it is read, and text left unsent in Claude's input box (never shown as read, never glued to the next message).
- [Terminal](docs/terminal.md): the real terminal, shared viewers and taking control.
- [Files](docs/files.md): browse an agent's folder, preview text, Markdown, images, PDFs and videos, download; which files a path in a conversation may open.
- [On a computer](docs/devices.md#on-a-computer): layout, terminal key bar and keyboard shortcuts.
- [On a phone](docs/devices.md#on-a-phone): touch controls and the phone keybar (order and hidden keys in Settings › Terminal).
- [On an iPad](docs/devices.md#on-an-ipad): the iPad layout.

## Project management

- [Getting started](docs/project-management.md#getting-started): the setup window, six steps from turning projects on to a first task; the coordinator's own memory.md (your decisions and preferences, kept across restarts and a change of agent); Finish setup on the board; New › Project (a typed, browsed or listed folder fills name and key, shown as ~/…; a wider sheet on a computer).
- [Projects](docs/project-management.md#projects): Settings › Projects, the project list and the project sheet's tabs (wide on a computer, General fields side by side).
- [General tab](docs/project-management.md#general): name, key (a new one also in wakes, notifications, logs, PR titles, `wherdr pm` outputs and new branches; texts written before the change read it too; former keys still work) and its badge color, base (working) branch, branch name template ({id}, {tag}, {type}, {slug}; default task/{id}; a branch the worker pushed is followed), agents, worktree setup (files copied from the clone such as .env, folders such as node_modules shared only while the lockfile matches the clone's, else a setup command with a time limit; the result in the task's log and the worker's instructions, a failure under Your turn with its output), repository visibility, allowed machines and their clone paths (each with its last readiness check, run again with ↻), Shown in (the home tab showing it: Automatic with its groups, paused machines left out unless a task runs there, a group, or All tabs; a hint without groups), placement (Heavy to the strongest, Balance the load, Home first; a task too big for every machine runs on the best one; an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the reserve holds the next ones; a worker started again is heavy only while its step takes screenshots).
- [Workflow tab](docs/project-management.md#workflow): how each task runs, its steps drawn in a row; task types (with an optional weight) and steps (a merge that pushes first waits up to a minute for GitHub; Bitbucket Cloud PRs: bitbucket.merge, credentials from the machine; a pipeline watch follows CI or a deploy and wakes the coordinator only on a failure), Edit as JSON, Save as template, Start over, review of the change the coordinator or Alfred proposed (one-line summary, who proposed it, your full request with a link back to it, readable or JSON), and its Workflow change card in the coordinator's conversation (steps before and after); the [reviewer fallback](docs/project-management.md#reviewer-fallback) (prefs reviewFallbackAgent and reviewFallbackModel, together, any pair, none by default, checked at Save, also under the project sheet's Agents): the reviewer started instead when the review agent's account is out of quota, before a start or mid-review (it reviews from the start), each switch in the log and on the Plan's review step, the review agent again once its quota is back.
- [Guards](docs/project-management.md#guards): protected branches, who may merge (a waiting merge goes on once wherdr may do it; one you merge on GitHub ends as merged; one cut by a restart goes on by itself), contributor PRs, the project sheet's in-app addresses.
- [Automations](docs/project-management.md#automations): tasks added on a schedule or an event.
- [Template library](docs/project-management.md#template-library): saved templates and examples, read, rename and delete; projects keep their own copy.
- [Who sends a wake](docs/project-management.md#who-sends-a-wake): each wake's first line and chat tag name its source: Autopilot, Step check (a held step's start, recheck or timeout, even with the autopilot off), Engine (a block given up after failed fixes), Health check (every 3h by default: done, waiting for you, stalled, idle machines; acked when all is well), Incident; in the conversation a wake is a compact muted row (tag, first reason, time; tap for the full text and turn, which ends at its own end or at your next message or `!`/`/` command), not a bubble, with the coordinator's last answer of that turn under it, muted; consecutive routine wakes fold into one row (3 routine checks, 08:00–11:00), an incident or an answer asking you stays visible in its stronger colour; routine events off by default, only judgment wakes the coordinator; one kind per wake, the same ack. Skipped, and listed by `autopilot show`: a scheduled wake while nothing it could act on changed, an Engine wake for a block that is only an offline or paused machine, a second wake for a question already answered with `tell`, a health check repeating the last one (12 h at most).
- [Autopilot](docs/project-management.md#autopilot): when the project works without you, each project's own (Alfred has none), the clock header button (no workflow proposals) and its window, its next wake, goal, wakes (the last on one line, the ones not handled highlighted, the full list under History) and limits (new projects: Tasks / day unlimited and At once Auto, pace and machine room still hold automatic work; limits and hours hold automatic work only: a start you ask for goes past them, with a word, and still counts; a hint on the older 10 / 2; Task added wakes only for tasks added by someone else than this coordinator); Keep the board busy: the engine starts the next to-do task itself while a machine has room; the coordinator's view of machines and weights (`autopilot show`; weights learned from measured memory peaks after 3 runs; `show <task>`, `--on`, `--weight`).
- [What a task's agent said](docs/project-management.md#what-a-tasks-agent-said): `wherdr pm read`, an agent's last message or question from any machine, and the question in the wake.
- [What agents show in the chat](docs/project-management.md#what-agents-show-in-the-chat): every agent's *Showing instead of telling* table (situation → tool, with an example): choices and task cards for all, plus highlights, status cards, action buttons, screenshots and proposed settings for Alfred and coordinators; one card per message, blocks only in a wake, the link after a refusal, never "done" before the card says so.
- [Board](docs/project-management.md#board): the project picker (Follow machine tab, the default once groups exist; All projects; one project; kept across devices), columns (a done or archived task is never under Your turn), cards (the id badge copies the id; the task's machine when its project allows several), time in the step and total time, Add task (with its weight: Auto, Light, Standard, Heavy), Start, Start on another machine (its readiness check), Stop, Delete; a refused merge said in plain words (a conflict the agent is already fixing leaves Your turn).
- [Board order](docs/project-management.md#board-order): cards in board order (the coordinator's `wherdr pm task order` first, then oldest first), shared by everyone and kept across restarts; Keep the board busy, the merge queue and `wherdr pm list` follow it.
- [Spec changes](docs/project-management.md#spec-changes): when you change your mind mid-task, the coordinator's `wherdr pm task edit` (title, description, reason, diff in the log), `task note` and `tell --spec`; the worker and the reviewer read every note, the latest overriding the description; shown under the description in the task sheet; never in a wake; after several send-backs, the coordinator's `task decide <task> pass` on findings that contradict a spec change its reason cites (date or words), never before a guarded merge nor on a critical finding, shown a day in Decisions.
- [Tasks that touch the same files](docs/project-management.md#tasks-that-touch-the-same-files): declared files (files.txt, task add --files), the start that waits behind a task with the same files, Start anyway.
- [Task sheet](docs/project-management.md#task-sheet): opens over the current page from Tasks to handle, Decisions or a chat task link (`?task=ID`, kept on reload); the id badge by the title (copies the id), time per step, waits for you, review rounds and CI fixes, the task's buttons (Check on GitHub, also `wherdr pm task check`, for a stuck merge step or an archived task's PR) and its Description (Markdown), Plan, History (the hand-offs between worker, reviewer, wherdr, the coordinator and you: reports, send-backs with their findings, fixes, catch-ups, CI fixes; Markdown, folded; on top a 3 to 6 line summary by Claude Haiku, made again on each new report or verdict, skipped while the pace holds automatic work) and Log tabs, in one scroll.
- [A task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab, Merge, Send back, Try again and other answers; a PR you merge on your Git host (I merged it, and what to do when it is not merged yet); Open the PR at the merge step for a PR a step gave as its link proof (GitHub, Bitbucket, GitLab, Azure DevOps), also on the card as PR #12; screenshots replaced after a rework (new commits since the review); a waiting PR kept up to date with its base, an approved merge that goes on by itself once ready (kept across updates, asked again only on new screenshots or interface changes; Merge stays loading on the card and the sheet until it merges or fails, with what it waits for, the same after a reload), and the project's merge queue (ready PRs merge in turn, a PR needing work steps out of line, updates only on a conflict or when GitHub requires them, all in one pass, idle agents released; its place or why it stepped out on the card); a tap on Your turn or Tasks to handle opens the asking agent's conversation, else the sheet; on a phone its buttons stay pinned at the bottom of the tab.
- [Notes on a task waiting for you](docs/project-management.md#notes-on-a-task-waiting-for-you): the To do tab's Worker's note (the closing report) and Reviewer's note (verdict, what was fixed during the rounds, what is left as minor), in Markdown, folded, with Show more, the task's summary above the worker's note, full width one above the other (Worker / Reviewer tabs on a phone).
- [Report a problem](docs/project-management.md#report-a-problem): tell the coordinator what is wrong with a task waiting for you, block its merge, withdraw.
- [What wherdr fixes on its own](docs/project-management.md#what-wherdr-fixes-on-its-own): a conflict with the base (to the worker), red CI (an infrastructure error in the log run again once, else to the worker), a push refused as behind its remote (synced, pushed again), an interrupted action (run again), a stalled agent; the coordinator woken once only after 2 failed tries, with what was tried.
- [A stalled task](docs/project-management.md#a-stalled-task): red CI or an idle agent: one nudge, a restart 10 min later, the coordinator woken 10 min after that, then Tasks to handle and a notification after 30 min; a stall or a step past its time limit leaves Tasks to handle once the task is back to work.
- [Why agents are gone](docs/project-management.md#why-agents-are-gone): the engine's cause from facts (machine offline, herdr-core or wherdr restarted, agent killed or crashed, out of memory, account limit, unknown), recorded as an incident per machine; `wherdr pm incidents [--since]`, the last open one in `autopilot show`.
- [The engine resumes the work](docs/project-management.md#the-engine-resumes-the-work): a task an incident stopped waits for wherdr (not Your turn) and is resumed once the cause is gone (restart or crash at once, machine back online, account limit reset): its worker in its worktree, Claude's conversation resumed, else a new agent with a handover; the tasks before it first, its followers *Waits for <task> to resume*; placement, room and pace held, one worker per task; the same cause again within an hour of a resume is not resumed again.
- [The incident wake](docs/project-management.md#the-incident-wake): one wake per incident (not per task) once the engine's resumes settle, to each project's coordinator and to Alfred for all projects: the cause and its evidence, what was resumed, what still waits and why (machine offline, limit until <time>), what needs the coordinator or the user; never state a cause not read: `wherdr pm incidents`, `autopilot show`, `read <task>` first, else 'unknown' and what was checked.
- [A task's temporary files](docs/project-management.md#a-tasks-temporary-files): `.wherdr-tmp` in the task's worktree (TMPDIR, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, NODE_COMPILE_CACHE), ignored by git, removed with the worktree; no agent started while /tmp has under 500 MB free.
- [Processes an agent leaves behind](docs/project-management.md#processes-an-agent-leaves-behind): ending an agent kills its terminal's process tree and groups (TERM, then KILL after 3 s); every 5 minutes and at start, processes an agent started (known by the task's .wherdr-tmp they inherit, never by their folder alone; on macOS, sh/zsh/sleep with their marked parent or group, or re-parented in the task's worktree; never the user's own shells, apps or daemons) are killed once their task has no live agent, and logged on the task; Settings › Machines says *n leftover processes killed*; the wherdr template's workers run test commands that could hang with a timeout.
- [Alfred's command](docs/alfred.md): `wherdr alfred`, what Alfred reads and changes after your yes (projects, their machines, guards, coordinators started or resumed, settings, v2 projects to set up), the workflow changes it proposes for your review, and its messages to a project's coordinator (`tell`, `last`).
- [Agents of a task that waits for you](docs/project-management.md#agents-of-a-task-that-waits-for-you): idle agents ended and started again, at once when you answer (a decision, Send back, Try again); a watchdog starts again the agent of a task under way missing for 3 minutes (after a restart too), else the card says why and the coordinator is woken once at the second failure; kept while the worker updates the PR (a catch-up, a CI fix), a worker that ended started again with that work (once), else the card says why it waits (its machine offline or paused, its agent ended) and the coordinator is woken (none: Your turn), unpushed commits pushed first; which agent a coordinator's `tell` reaches (--to worker|reviewer); in a wake, `tell --fix base|ci|machine|stall --reason` unblocks a mechanical block (autopilot on, twice per task and step, logged), a permission request stays yours; a failed step action handed over with `--fix` leaves Tasks to handle (*the agent is fixing it*), is tried again once the worker is done, and comes back with the new reason if it fails again or the worker stops without a report. One worker and one reviewer per task: a second start at once is refused (already starting), a held start dropped, a duplicate agent ended and logged.
- [After an update](docs/alfred.md#after-an-update): new instructions for Alfred and coordinators, and the one-line notice on their next command.

## Machines, quotas and notifications

- [Several machines](docs/machines.md#several-machines-ssh): machines reached by hc over SSH.
- [Before adding a machine](docs/machines.md#before-adding-a-machine): what a machine needs first.
- [Manage machines](docs/machines.md#manage-machines): Settings › Machines (one card per machine: name, state, actions, keep awake, memory), add, reconnect, rename, forget, keep awake (until a time or turned off, laptop battery and lid warning), capacity (memory, cores, load on Linux and macOS; swap on Linux, memory pressure on macOS), memory limits (an idle machine always takes one task its RAM holds, the minimum free holds the next ones), available hours and offline machines, and where each start goes (placement across a project's machines).
- [Pause a machine for a project](docs/machines.md#pause-a-machine-for-a-project): a machine's on/off switch in a project's Machines list: no new task there, running ones finish, clone kept; Paused in every project in Settings › Machines.
- [Claude and Codex quotas](docs/quotas.md#claude-and-codex-quotas): remaining usage per account, with the machines sharing it, and its setup; a Codex 'Limit reached' past its reset reads as reset, credits show and let work go on, an old reading says how to refresh it.
- [Pace](docs/quotas.md#pace): Settings › Agents › Pace, its modes (Free, the default, stops only at the account's own limit), when automatic work may start, and the end-of-week burn (one switch: no pace limit until the weekly reset, then off).
- [Notifications](docs/notifications.md#notifications): Web Push and Do not disturb.
- [A default and exceptions](docs/notifications.md#a-default-and-exceptions): one synced policy: a default and its exceptions, a coordinator's kept across restarts.
- [Notifications on hc](docs/core.md#notifications): when v3 sends a push, from hc's events.

## Extending and fixing

- [Plugins](docs/plugins.md#wherdr-plugins): optional page plugins and how to install them.
- [The plugin module](docs/plugins.md#the-module): what a plugin file exports.
- [Markers](docs/plugins.md#markers-data-wherdr): `data-wherdr` markers a plugin can find.
- [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#troubleshooting): hc connection, conversations, machines and network problems.
- [Setup on hc](docs/core.md#setup): `HC_SOCKET`, the hc endpoint wherdr talks to.

## Contributors

- [Development and tests](docs/development.md): run from source and test.
- [Design rules](docs/design.md): the interface styling reference, sheets included (where focus goes on open); nothing scrolls sideways (no negative horizontal margin without an `overflow-safe` reason); one scroll per sheet; the app's thin scrollbars, never the browser's.
- [Dictation design](docs/dictation.md): the dictation engines and how to add one; the on-device model cards (each model's best languages and their quality, the device's language marked); why a server-side model install fails (bzip2 missing, disk full); read aloud and its voices (iOS gives web apps only its standard voices); the neural voice catalog (Siwis, Cori, MLS) and its engine (streamed WebAudio playback, fallback to the device's voices); the Voice of wherdr setting (install a French or English voice, each reply read in its guessed language).
- [Read aloud: the voice of wherdr](docs/read-aloud.md): the on-device voices (Siwis, Cori, MLS), their licences and the attribution shown; espeak-ng (GPL) inside the pinned sherpa-onnx 1.12.x runtime; the memory budget (measured heap, else an estimate); the iPhone 13 measurements of Siwis and Cori (load, first sentence, real-time factor; Heap is the runtime's 512 MiB WASM memory, not the voice's own use); how to measure with Test (download, load, first sentence, real-time factor, heap).

## v2 only

- [The wherdr command](docs/command.md): the 2.x npm and Homebrew packages and service.
- [Migrate from a 1.x Docker install](docs/migrate-from-1.x-docker.md): Docker to the native 2.0 service.
- [Releasing](docs/RELEASING.md): release process of 2.x (npm, Homebrew) and 3.x (GitHub release only), and the v2 → v3 transition checklist.
